text:
Darian: Heads-up — overnight we saw a sharp spike of Xid 31 and Xid 13 on a subset of A10 nodes in us-west-2 (rack r12b). Started ~02:10 local time, ~250 Xid events in 30m.
SRE-Bot: alert: gpu_xid_rate_high rack=r12b codes=[31,13] count=250 window=30m
Anya: linking the telemetry I ran this morning — the spike lines up with heavy embedding batch jobs from tenant-echo and a couple of sampling jobs from tenant-lens.
Lee: did autoscaler do anything weird? any pod churn that could stress PCIe or driver state?
Darian: yes — autoscaler triggered scale-up at 02:05 and a few nodes were drained/evicted. Not huge churn but correlated timing.
Tess: posting relevant dmesg snippet from one affected host (truncated):

```
[ 4001.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Channel 00000000
[ 4001.123459] GPU 0000:65:00:00: Ecc errors corrected: L1 0 L2 12
[ 4001.123462] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, Channel 00000003
```

Jun: interesting that L2 corrected ECC jumped right before Xid spikes — could be thermal / power line noise or bad memory cell being exercised by a workload pattern.
Anya: I pulled per-tenant telemetry: tenant-echo embedder jobs increased batch_size to 64 for a short window and switched to int8 quant set. Before change, their error rate was nil.
Darian: tenant-lens was doing high-concurrency sampling (streaming with many short requests) — a mix of small sequence lengths but >8 concurrent streams per GPU.
Lee: possible hypothesis: int8 quantized embedder with larger batches increases memory access pattern and ECC exposure; at the same time concurrent sampling creates sudden kernel preemption, exposing a driver race leading to Xid 31.
Tess: nv-host logs show repeated soft reset attempts on GPU 65:00:00, then one hard reset. I saved /var/log/nvidia-host-65-00-00.log to infra artifact store (path: s3://infra-artifacts/xid/1939001234/host-65-00-00.log)
SRE-Bot: ticket created INF-4721 assigned -> darian; linked logs: s3://infra-artifacts/xid/1939001234
Anya: quick repro plan: reproduce tenant-echo batch_size=64 int8 embedder profile on a non-prod A10. Run concurrent sampling from tenant-lens profile (8+ streams) and monitor ECC counters + nvml for Xid events.
Jun: can we also repro with and without CPU core isolation? suspect IRQ handling may influence.
Darian: doing an initial repro on staging now. If it reproduces, we'll try driver 560.xx vs 590.xx to see whether kernel/driver changes alter failure rate.
Tess: FYI we already have a history of transient Xid 31 on this rack flagged last quarter — but frequency was much lower. Might be a card degrading.
Lee: ops suggestion: drain the most affected host (gpu 65:00:00) and move pods off until we get dump and vendor triage. If repro in staging, escalate hardware RMA.
Anya: I'll instrument the repro with a small cron that toggles batch_size to see threshold. Also add per-job nvml ECC readouts to our trace logs.
Darian: I've manually placed a soft-drain on node r12b-host-17 (contains GPU 65:00:00) and set replace=yes in node annotation. Will keep it in soft-drain to collect artifacts before full replace.
SRE-Bot: action: node r12b-host-17 set soft-drain by darian
Jun: for triage notes — capture these: dmesg Xid lines, /var/log/nvidia-host, `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,POWER,UTILIZATION`, `kubectl describe pod` around eviction, and kernel oops if any.
Tess: should we throttle tenant-echo on production until we know more? cost vs availability question.
Darian: recommended: temporary policy limit to embedder batch_size 64 for tenant-echo for 24h, or route them to a dedicated pool that is isolated from high-concurrency sampling tenants.
Anya: also a quick model-level mitigation: force fp16 (no int8) on embedder profile until vendor completes RMA/driver analysis. That reduces memory stress.
Lee: I'll coordinate with capacity planning — if we need to cordon additional hosts that's fine but want to avoid large capacity churn during day.
Jun: next steps summary: 1) reproduce in staging (Anya/Darian) 2) collect full nv-host logs + ECC timeline (Tess) 3) soft-drain and preserve artifacts (Darian) 4) vendor RMA if hw shows persistent ECC growth (ops). Also consider temporary policy change for tenant-echo.
Darian: adding all artifacts to ticket INF-4721 with steps to reproduce, logs, and timelines. Will ping vendor rep if staging repro happens.
Tess: noted. I pushed a quick monitoring alert tweak to surface L2 ECC > 10 in 10m for those racks.
Anya: re: correlation analysis — I'll run a short script to compute tenant-weighted Xid density and send a heatmap. Early look: tenant-echo responsible for ~72% of windowed Xid events.
Lee: thanks folks. Keep updates in thread. :thumbsup:
Darian: update 02:50 — repro succeeded on staging with int8+batch64+8streams; saw 15 Xid events in 12 minutes. Uploading traces.
SRE-Bot: note: follow-up scheduled 10:00 UTC vendor call; invite sent to infra, runtime, and tenant engineering leads.
Anya: FYI tenant-echo engineering acknowledged and already rolling a quick profile change to fp16 in prod rampdown window.
Darian: closing loop for now — leaving node soft-drained, vendor triage in progress. Will update ticket INF-4721 with RMA decision tomorrow.
